hardware_findings.observation: The generated banner drew all 48 pre-separator runs and then stopped before the separator, subtitle and row-9 prompt.
After replacing the unavailable bulk primitive, the separator, subtitle and prompt completed, but raw screen codes 77 and 78 rendered as M and N in the canonical mixed-case charset.

root_causes.summary: The dialect registry exposes CALLPRIM 12, but the canonical Workbench enables LISP65_VM_SCREEN_PRIMS without LISP65_SCREEN_WRITE_STRING. The P0 oracle implemented the call unconditionally, so it proved a capability the product profile did not contain.

The banner specification assigned diagonal graphics to screen codes 77 and 78. Those glyphs exist in the uppercase/graphics charset; the Workbench deliberately uses the mixed-case charset where the same codes are uppercase M and N.

rejected_alternative.option: enable LISP65_SCREEN_WRITE_STRING in the resident Workbench
rejected_alternative.reason: The isolated product probe violates the post-boot reserve, overlay VMA, transport-window and multiple runtime-slice stack-safe gates. Expanding the resident screen surface is not a small banner correction.

mechanism: The banner uses only screen-put-char, poke, string-ref and write-char capabilities present in the canonical Workbench.
A dedicated %banner-separator entry colors 66 cells through screen-put-char and publishes raw horizontal-line code 64 through the pinned $0800/80-column contract.
The subtitle uses 22 screen-put-char calls instead of unavailable CALLPRIM 12.
The lambda keeps the normative run coordinates but uses yellow reverse-space cells, making the glyph independent of the active charset.
